history: The Parlamento is a place to talk, and the word makes the point. Its first part is the verb parlare. That verb does not come from Latin loqui, ‘to speak’, the usual verb of the classical period, but from Late Latin parabolare. Parabola began as Greek parabolē, a comparison or story, such as the parables of the Gospels, and in Late Latin it came to mean any ‘speech’, then ‘a word’, and then parabolare, ‘to speak’. From there come Italian parlare, French parler and Spanish palabra, ‘word’. In the Middle Ages the French noun parlement meant ‘a talk, a meeting’, and later a council of nobles. Italian uses Parlamento for the national legislature: la Camera and il Senato.
